title: BattlEye client emulation: a 2020 boundary-of-trust case study
summary: vmcall's BottlEye write-up makes the game-to-anti-cheat client interface visible and argues that historical server exchanges could be satisfied without the expected local components. Its demonstrated outcomes are tied to 2020 integrations, not a general present-day bypass claim.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: BEClient is an integration boundary between the game and BattlEye; the article examines what server-visible communication demonstrated about local trust.
A historically accepted client exchange does not establish that the service or driver was authentic.
Game-specific protocol variations and subsequent changes prevent extrapolating the 2020 demonstration to current games.
